key_insight: Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP) separates understanding a robot task from learning how to execute it: pretraining supplies scene and task knowledge, while simulation teaches robot control.
problem_solved: Robot policies must connect language and visual understanding to physical actions, including when familiar concepts appear in new combinations.
method: Use a pretrained 27B-parameter model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning.
Teach an off-the-shelf vision-language model to control a robot through a simple tool harness.
Apply supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO reinforcement learning on simple simulated tasks to develop movement skills.
impact: ZAP offers a recipe for combining pretrained understanding with simulation-based control training. For practitioners, it suggests a path toward compositional robot skills without relying on real-world robot training data, though the abstract provides no quantitative results.
visual_elements: Split-panel illustration: pretraining learns “what,” simulation teaches “how.”
Training pipeline: pretrained understanding → supervised fine-tuning → GRPO in simulation → robot actions.
Tool-harness diagram linking visual observations and task instructions to robot control commands.
Concept grid showing familiar objects, instructions, and actions recombined into new tasks.
paper_title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
paper_authors: Benjamin Pikus, Daniel Saunders, Mircea Mironenco, Salman Mohammadi, Mathew Mathew
